append.text: **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:10, 38:22 DO) *vadam ad portas ínferi* → *irei às portas do inferno*; *non inférnus confitébitur tibi* → *o inferno não vos dará graças*** (the genitive as 48:16, 88:49; the nominative as 6:6, which the verse echoes). The ambiguity reader heard 'hell, the place of the damned' at both. Mt 16:18 *portæ inferi* is *as forças do Inferno* even in the CNBB Bible; the CNBB LH and Lectionary paraphrase *a mansão triste dos mortos* (ps222/circulation.md). Options *dos infernos* (212's plural), *da morada / mansão dos mortos*. Passed the v2 gate.

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:20 DO) *corrípies me, et vivificábis me* → *vós me castigareis e me vivificareis*** (= 137:7, 142:11a; DO's Tuesday Lauds II antiphon). The ambiguity reader listed *vivificareis* unknown again.
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:13 DO) *quasi tabernáculum pastórum* → *como uma tenda de pastores*** (the plural kept against the LH's *de um pastor*).

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:12 DO) *habitatórem quiétis* → *o habitante do repouso*** — *quies*, not in the psalter, takes the *réquies* word (one root for the pair; MS1932 the same). Who dwells in rest (the living at peace, the dead) is left open, as in the Latin; the ambiguity reader could not tell. Options *descanso*, *sossego*.

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:16 DO) *meditábor ut colúmba* → *meditarei como a pomba*** — the dove's murmur (Hebrew *hāgâ*); DRB keeps *meditate*. The ambiguity reader found it odd for a dove; kept. *gemerei* (MS1932, the LH) the option.

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:14 = 38:16 DO) *fínies me* → *vós acabareis comigo*** — *finíre*, the row's idiom; *vós* supplied in v2 because the ambiguity reader heard a plural 'you' with no addressee (the canticle's first second person).

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:19 Vulg.; DO 38:23) *pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam* → *o pai fará conhecer aos filhos a vossa verdade*** (the row). The v1 stylist asked *dará a conhecer* — the fourth stylist to ask it (97, 144, 221, 222).

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:14 Vulg.; DO 38:17) *suspiciéntes in excélsum* → *olhando para o alto*** — a direction (*in* + accusative), after 72:8's *no alto*; MS1932, DM1962 the same. *para a altura* the option.

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:17 Vulg.; DO 38:21) *Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret* → *Vós, porém, libertastes a minha alma*** — no source named, so *libertar* (6:5, 68:19, 118:153); the Lectionary's refrain says *livrastes*.
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:10 Vulg.; DO 38:11) *Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum* → *Busquei o resto dos meus anos*** (Jerome's reading, not the Hebrew's 'I am deprived'; MS1932's words).
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:13 Vulg.; DO 38:15) *quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea* → *como um leão, assim quebrou todos os meus ossos*.**
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:14 Vulg.; DO 38:16) *sicut pullus hirúndinis* → *como o filhote da andorinha*.**
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:18 Vulg.; DO 38:22) *qui descéndunt in lacum* → *os que descem à cova*** (the formula).

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:20 Vulg.; DO 38:24) *psalmos nostros cantábimus* → *cantaremos os nossos salmos*** — the Latin's own *cantáre psalmos*, not *psállere*, so not *entoar salmos*; the CNBB LH has the same words.

**Collision, for Gustavo: canticle 222 (Isa 38:12 Vulg.; DO 38:14) *succídit me* → *ceifou-me*** takes this row's *ceifar* for another Latin verb (*succīdo*, 'cut from below, fell, mow'), to keep it apart from *præcídere → cortar* in the same colon. See the *succídere* row.
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:13 Vulg.; DO 38:15) *Sperábam usque ad mane* → *Eu esperava até a manhã*** (no object; the ambiguity reader heard 'waited').

**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:11 Vulg.; DO 38:12) *Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, et habitatórem quiétis* → *Não olharei mais o homem, nem o habitante do repouso*** — transitive, as canticle 212; v1's *olhar para … para o* the stylist heard padded. *verei* (MS1932, the stylist) refused: it merges with *vidébo* one line before.
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:10 Vulg.) *In dimídio diérum meórum* → *No meio dos meus dias*** (the same four words; rule 6).
**Canticle 222 (Isa 38:20 Vulg.; DO 38:24) *Dómine, salvum me fac* → *Senhor, salvai-me*.**

terms: | succídere (*succídit me*, long i) | ceifar (*enquanto eu ainda urdia, ceifou-me*) | open — **for Gustavo** | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:12 Vulg.; DO 38:14)**; not a psalter word. DO's accent gives *succīdo* < *sub-cædo*, 'cut from below, fell; mow, reap' (L&S), not *succĭdo* 'sink'. Kept apart from *præcídere → cortar* in the same colon; collides with *métere → ceifar* (125:5). The ambiguity reader listed *ceifou-me* unknown; passed the v2 gate. *cortou-me* (MS1932, DRB) the option; *abateu-me* heard as 'discouraged'. |

| ordíri | urdir (*enquanto eu ainda urdia*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:12 Vulg.; DO 38:14)**; to lay the warp (L&S); the weaver of the same colon. The ambiguity reader listed *urdia* unknown and heard 'plotting' possible; kept. |

| convólvere (*convolúta est a me*) | enrolar (*e enrolada longe de mim*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:12 Vulg.; DO 38:13)**; the struck tent. v1 *para longe de mim*, a calque to the stylist; the v2 Latinist (minor) found *longe* a distance the Latin does not state and asked *e enrolada e tirada de mim*, held as an option (it says *auférre*'s *tirar* twice). |

| attenuáre (*óculi*) | definhar (*Os meus olhos definharam*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:14 Vulg.; DO 38:17)**; 'make thin'. A third verb for failing eyes, kept apart from *defícere → desfalecer* (68:4, 118:82) and *languére → enfraquecer-se* (87:9b). *se cansaram* (MS1932, DM1962, the LH) is *laboráre*'s. |

| recogitáre (+ dat.) | repassar diante de (*Repassarei diante de vós todos os meus anos*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:15 Vulg.; DO 38:19)**; 'think over again'; MS1932's verb and preposition. *para vós* the bare dative, option. |

| amaríssimus | amaríssimo (*a minha amargura amaríssima*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:17 Vulg.; DO 38:20) *Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima* → *Eis, em paz a minha amargura amaríssima*** — verbless, as the Latin, whose two readings (bitter in peace / turned to peace) stay open. The ambiguity reader listed *amaríssima* unknown; *amarguíssima* the option. |
| vim páti | sofrer violência (*Senhor, sofro violência, respondei por mim*) | open | **Canticle 222 (Isa 38:14 Vulg.; DO 38:18)**; after 37:12b *vim faciébant → faziam violência*. |
